title: Choose the fleet dashboard
question: One world for the captain’s phone and laptop. Keep this, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Punched Pixel Leaves
options.lineage: A tabbed reference board, redrawn as a pixel grid
options.thesis: One leaf is open and readable. Health, fleet, and chat are leaves you hinge between, not a pile of cards.
options.viewport: A standard tab bar across the top. The open leaf is fleet health: usage and API balances as chunky meters, and one vermilion slip when something is waiting on you. Alice is a tab, not a footer.
options.risk: If the hinge is slow, a live fleet feels filed in a book.

raised.raise: Agent state is a one-pixel detent, not a soft pill.
The one hold waiting on you wears a single ring.
Only the open leaf is full strength; the other sections sit one ply down.

options.label: Pocket Status Screen
options.thesis: The phone is the console. Health is a title screen of pixel sprites; the laptop is the same screen, wider.
options.viewport: Four agent sprites and their state across the top. Usage meters under them. Tap an agent and chat replaces the field. Phone is the same stack, one column.
options.risk: This is the look most pixel dashboards already ship. Familiar, and easy to stop at costume.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Projects and agents are rows. When state changes, the letters clack. The shell stays a normal dashboard.
options.viewport: A flap board of in-flight tasks leads. Usage sits in a side column. Tabs stay ordinary. A change from the bus flips one row, character by character.
options.case: A captain already reads a fleet as departures. Rows keep every current fact scannable.
options.risk: Flap motion on every SSE tick will feel noisy if it is not limited to real state changes.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Pixel type does the shouting. The same face is huge for “waiting on you” and small for the numbers under it.
options.viewport: One bitmap headline states the fleet in a sentence. Under it, ordinary tables for usage, tasks, and agents. Phone keeps the headline and one table.
options.case: This is pixel art as type, so the dashboard still reads as a tool. Phone scale is the same face, fewer columns.
options.risk: A poster headline can shove the actual controls below the fold.

options.label: Next Gate
options.thesis: The one thing that needs you is a yellow band with a huge label. Everything else is the corridor under it.
options.viewport: A sticky yellow band names the live hold or “clear”. Below it, standard panels for usage, fleet, and agents. On a phone the band is the whole first screen, with one next action.
options.case: The captain’s job is often one decision. The band keeps that decision from hiding in a badge.
options.risk: When nothing is waiting, the giant band has nothing honest to say.

options.label: Centre Rail
options.case: A captain does not open this to read an edition. The rail would hide chat and meters.
options.kept: State marks are one device pixel, filled when pressed.
options.viewport: Two text columns and a vermilion key rail.

options.label: Night Chart
options.lineage: A star atlas under a red lamp
options.case: Dots cannot carry balances, chat, or start and stop.
options.kept: Whatever is waiting on you is the only thing ringed.

options.label: Title Wall
options.case: Agents are not shows. Artwork would replace the numbers.
options.kept: One section is in focus; the others step back.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean admin dashboard: side nav, cards, tables, one accent.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav for agents. Main column for usage and fleet. Chat in the selected agent. Phone collapses the nav to a tab bar.
canonCard.risk: It will look like every other local admin tool.
